title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: What the Market Is Pricing In — Valuation, ADR Parity & Peer Comps
question: Why does SKHY trade at 8.56x trailing P/E and 3.25x forward P/E yet 5.53x P/B, and how does the NASDAQ ADR price reconcile with KRX 000660?

epigraph.quote: In memory semiconductors, a low P/E on peak earnings is rarely a bargain, and a high P/B at the top of the cycle demands forensic proof of structural earnings power.
epigraph.author: Semiconductor Cycle Valuation Maxim

web_blocks.html: Any institutional underwriting of SKHY must begin by resolving a glaring data discrepancy between U.S. quote feeds [21, 22]. On November 13, 2026, Finviz reports SKHY's market capitalization at $960.57B and enterprise value at $917.61B, while TradingView lists market capitalization at $660.29B [21, 22]. The gap is not a data bug; it is the mechanics of the 1:10 American Depositary Share (ADS) structure combined with a steep U.S. listing premium [4, 21, 23]. Each NASDAQ SKHY ADS represents one-tenth of one ordinary KRX:000660 share (10 ADSs = 1 common share) [4, 6]. Across approximately 729 million ordinary shares (7.29B ADS equivalents), multiplying 7.29B by the $131.79 ADR close yields $960.75B [21]. Meanwhile, on the Korea Exchange, 000660 traded around KRW 1,216,000–1,289,000 (~KRW 1,250,000 midpoint) with USD/KRW at 1,361.89, implying a local equity value near KRW 899T–911T, or ~$660B USD [22, 23, 24].

web_blocks.caption: SKHY NASDAQ ADR vs. KRX:000660 Ordinary Parity Reconciliation (as of 2026-11-13)
rows: U.S. ADR buyers pay a ~44%–45% scarcity premium over Seoul parity [21].
10 ADSs at $131.79 equal KRW 1,794,835 vs. ~KRW 1,250,000 local close [22, 23, 24].
web_blocks.takeaway: U.S. ADR investors at $131.79 are paying roughly 44% above Korean ordinary share parity due to restricted cross-border fungibility and U.S. AI-index demand.

web_blocks.html: This parity gap matters directly for downside risk [21, 23]. At $131.79, 10 ADSs translate to KRW 1,794,835 at the 1,361.89 spot rate, representing a 43.6% premium over local KRX shares [23, 24]. If cross-border arbitrage expands or U.S. risk appetite cools, the ADR can compress toward KRX parity (~$91.80 per ADS) even if Seoul fundamentals remain intact [21, 23].

web_blocks.title: Peer Valuation Matrix: Memory, Storage & AI Foundry Comps

web_blocks.html: Comparing SKHY against its direct memory rival Micron (MU), enterprise storage peers Western Digital (WDC) and Seagate (STX), foundry partner TSMC (TSM), and anchor customer NVIDIA (NVDA) reveals a classic cyclical valuation split [21, 22]. On headline earnings multiples, SKHY trades at 8.56x trailing P/E and 3.25x forward P/E—nearly identical to Micron's 10.49x trailing and 3.69x forward P/E, and far below TSMC (17.26x forward) and NVIDIA (10.34x forward) [21, 22]. Yet on enterprise-value-to-EBITDA (9.39x) and price-to-book (5.53x), SKHY commands a premium to its own historical cycle because its 74.52% operating margin and 71.84% ROIC sit at generational highs [21, 25].

web_blocks.caption: Live Peer Valuation & Profitability Snapshot (as of 2026-11-13)
web_blocks.takeaway: SKHY and MU trade at single-digit trailing and forward P/Es despite >70% operating margins, signaling market skepticism about cycle durability.

web_blocks.html: Notice how every memory and storage name in the peer group (SKHY, MU, WDC, STX) trades at forward P/E multiples between 3.25x and 7.94x, alongside PEG ratios of 0.03 to 0.10 [21]. The market is not ignoring SK hynix's 209.28% TTM revenue growth or 74.52% operating margin [21]. Rather, institutional capital refuses to capitalize peak memory margins at a 20x secular multiple [25].

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF & Historical Memory Valuation Bands

web_blocks.html: A Reverse DCF clarifies what $131.79 requires [21]. With Finviz Enterprise Value at $917.61B, a 10.5% WACC (reflecting the 5.10% 10-year U.S. Treasury yield plus a 5.4% equity risk premium), and a 3.0% terminal growth rate, the market is pricing in roughly $68.8B of steady-state annual free cash flow in perpetuity [21]. In FY2025, SK hynix generated approximately KRW 24.68T (~$18.1B) in free cash flow [1]. Even though Q1–Q3 2026 operating profit exploded to KRW 181.48T, sustaining $68.8B of annual FCF after ~30% fab capex reinvestment requires AI HBM demand and pricing to remain elevated without a traditional memory downturn [1, 2, 13, 26].

web_blocks.caption: SK hynix Historical Memory Cycle Valuation Bands vs. November 2026
rows: Market compressed P/B below 1.0x ahead of the 2019–2020 inventory glut [1, 25].
Trough losses gave way to an AI HBM re-rating before profits recovered [1, 25].
HBM3E dominance and >40% ROE drove a structural re-rating above 3.5x book [1, 25].
Consensus sees FY26 rev KRW 259T–278T and FY27 growth, yet ADR P/B sits at 5.53x [21, 25, 26].
web_blocks.takeaway: While 3.25x forward P/E looks optically cheap, SKHY's 5.53x ADR P/B (and ~3.85x local KRX P/B) sits well above historical memory-cycle norms.

web_blocks.html: Street consensus still projects strong top-line momentum, with FY2026 revenue estimated at KRW 259T–278T (~$190B–$204B) and FY2027 revenue climbing toward KRW 290T–300T+ backed by >50% LTA coverage [13, 26]. Finviz lists a consensus sell-side target price of $264.30 (1.36 Buy rating) [21]. However, history shows that memory multiples contract before earnings peak, and the 44% ADR premium leaves zero margin of safety if HBM4 pricing or hyperscaler capex moderates [23, 25].

web_blocks.title: FCF Sensitivity & Why Peak-Cycle EBITDA Overstates Owner Earnings

web_blocks.html: A subtle trap in semiconductor valuation is relying on EV/EBITDA (9.39x) when capital intensity is rising [1, 21]. In FY2025, SK hynix booked KRW 13.93T in depreciation and amortization but spent KRW 28.60T on fab capex—more than double its D&A charge [1]. As Cheongju M15X, Yongin, and the West Lafayette packaging facility scale into 2027, capex near 30% of revenue keeps owner free cash flow well below accounting net income [10, 18, 19]. Even if mid-cycle FCF reaches $60B—more than triple FY2025's ~$18.1B—a 12x cyclical multiple implies $763B equity value ($104.66/ADR), or 20.6% below CMP [1, 21]. Blending that $104.66 mid-cycle FCF anchor 50/50 with a $145.00 HBM4 cycle-extension multiple sets our reconciled Base Case target at $125.00 (-5.2% vs. CMP) [21, 22].

book_paragraphs: To understand why SK hynix trades at $131.79 on the NASDAQ—down 34.06% from its $199.87 post-IPO high yet still priced at $960.57 billion on U.S. quote screens—you have to untangle two separate puzzles: an ADR structural premium and the classic optical illusion of peak-cycle memory multiples.

Start with the share-count puzzle. If you pull up Finviz on November 13, 2026, it shows a market capitalization of $960.57 billion and an enterprise value of $917.61 billion, backed by 7.29 billion shares outstanding. Pull up TradingView on the same day, however, and it reports a market capitalization of $660.29 billion. Which number is right? Both are mathematically consistent, because they measure two different markets separated by a 1:10 depositary ratio and imperfect cross-border arbitrage.

When SK hynix listed on the NASDAQ in July 2026, each American Depositary Share was structured to represent one-tenth of an ordinary share traded on the Korea Exchange under ticker 000660. Since SK hynix has roughly 710 million to 729 million ordinary shares outstanding in Seoul, that translates to 7.29 billion ADS equivalents. Multiply 7.29 billion by the $131.79 NASDAQ close and you get $960.75 billion. Meanwhile, in Seoul, 000660 traded around 1.25 million won per share with the U.S. dollar at 1,361.89 won—equating to roughly $660.29 billion in total local market value. Put differently, ten NASDAQ ADSs at $131.79 cost $1,317.90, or nearly 1.80 million won—a 43.6% premium over buying the exact same underlying economic claim in Seoul.

That 43.6% ADS premium is a critical risk factor for U.S. investors. It exists because domestic Korean shares are not freely fungible into NASDAQ ADSs without regulatory and custodian friction, and U.S. AI-focused funds bid up the liquid U.S. ticker during the summer 2026 euphoria. When risk appetite reverses, as it did in autumn 2026, that premium can deflate alongside the underlying stock. If the ADR premium were to collapse completely back to Seoul parity at 1.25 million won, SKHY would trade near $91.80 per share—without a single change to SK hynix's earnings.

The second puzzle is why SKHY trades at just 8.56 times trailing earnings and 3.25 times forward consensus earnings. On the surface, a business growing trailing revenue by 209.28% with a 74.52% operating margin and 71.84% return on invested capital at 3.25 times forward earnings looks like the bargain of a lifetime. Yet look across the peer group on November 13, 2026: Micron trades at 10.49 times trailing earnings and 3.69 times forward earnings. Western Digital trades at 7.31 times forward earnings. Seagate trades at 7.94 times forward earnings. Even NVIDIA trades at 10.34 times forward earnings, while TSMC commands 17.26 times.

Why does the market refuse to pay 20 times earnings for SK hynix? Because in memory semiconductors, single-digit P/E ratios appear at the peak of the cycle, not the bottom. In 2018, at the peak of the cloud server DRAM boom, SK hynix earned a 51.5% operating margin, yet its price-to-book ratio compressed to 0.88x by year-end because institutional investors anticipated the 2019–2020 oversupply. Conversely, in 2023, when SK hynix posted a massive operating loss of minus 7.73 trillion won, its price-to-book ratio expanded to 1.87x because the market was pricing in the upcoming HBM recovery.

Today, SKHY's price-to-book ratio sits at 5.53x on the NASDAQ ADR (and roughly 3.85x on Seoul ordinary parity), compared to its 2025 average of 3.70x to 3.86x and its 2018–2023 cycle range of 0.80x to 1.87x. A Reverse DCF confirms how high the bar has been set: at a $917.61 billion enterprise value, a 10.5% discount rate (anchored by a 5.10% 10-year Treasury yield), and a 3.0% terminal growth rate, the ADR price assumes SK hynix generates roughly $68.8 billion in steady-state annual free cash flow forever. In FY2025, full-year free cash flow was roughly 24.68 trillion won, or $18.1 billion. Even with Q1–Q3 2026 operating profit surging to 181.48 trillion won, sustaining $68.8 billion of annual FCF through the next fab capex wave leaves little room for error.

book_subsections.title: Consensus Forecasts vs. The Valuation Trap
paragraphs: Sell-side consensus remains overwhelmingly bullish on SK hynix's near-term earnings trajectory. Trackers project FY2026 revenue of 259 trillion to 278 trillion won and FY2027 revenue exceeding 290 trillion to 300 trillion won, supported by long-term supply agreements covering more than half of 2027–2028 HBM capacity. Consensus local EPS is modeled around 26,310 won for FY2026 and 33,100 won for FY2027, while Finviz reflects an average analyst target price of $264.30—exactly double the current $131.79 quote.

However, our underwriting discipline separates earnings momentum from valuation safety. When a cyclical hardware business trades at 5.53 times book value and a 43.6% premium to its home-market listing, consensus price targets based on peak-cycle EBITDA multiples offer false comfort. Any normalization in HBM4 gross margins as Samsung and Micron ramp, or any pause in hyperscaler AI capex, would compress both the forward earnings estimate and the price-to-book multiple simultaneously.

Consider the sensitivity math. Even if SK hynix delivers $60 billion of mid-cycle free cash flow—more than triple its FY2025 level—capitalizing that at a 12x cyclical FCF multiple yields $720 billion of enterprise value, or roughly $763 billion in equity value after adding $42.96 billion of net cash. Across 7.29 billion ADS equivalents, that equates to $104.66 per ADR, which is 20.6% below today's $131.79 close. Blending that $104.66 mid-cycle FCF anchor 50/50 with a $145.00 HBM4 cycle-extension multiple sets our reconciled 12-month Base Case target at $125.00. Only if AI memory behaves like a true zero-cyclicality software monopoly does $131.79 look cheap on intrinsic cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Why EV/EBITDA and P/FCF Tell Different Stories
paragraphs: A final nuance in SKHY's valuation card is the divergence between its 9.39x EV/EBITDA and 15.36x trailing P/FCF. Because semiconductor fabs depreciate rapidly—depreciation and amortization ran 13.93 trillion won in FY2025—EBITDA overstates owner earnings whenever capex exceeds depreciation. In FY2025, SK hynix spent roughly 28.60 trillion won on capital expenditures, more than double its depreciation charge, to build out M15X in Cheongju and early Yongin infrastructure. As Yongin and the Indiana packaging plant scale into 2027, capex intensity near 30% of revenue will keep free cash flow conversion well below accounting net income.

book_subsections.title: Peer Relative Valuation: Why TSMC and Micron Frame the Ceiling
paragraphs: Looking closely at our six-company peer table sharpens the relative value picture. Micron, SK hynix's closest pure-play memory rival, trades at $778.31 for an $880.6 billion market cap, 10.49x trailing P/E, 3.69x forward P/E, 7.70x EV/EBITDA, and 14.93x P/FCF, with a 75.01% operating margin and 59.39% ROIC. In other words, Micron offers nearly identical margins and a slightly cheaper EV/EBITDA and P/FCF without any cross-border ADR premium.

Meanwhile, TSMC trades at 25.66x trailing P/E and 17.26x forward P/E on a 57.78% operating margin and 32.67% ROIC because foundry logic enjoys structural multi-customer pricing power without commodity DRAM inventory cycles. SKHY's 5.53x ADR price-to-book already prices it halfway toward a secular foundry multiple, even though its underlying business remains tied to memory capacity cycles. Until either the ADR premium narrows or the market proves that HBM4 pricing can hold through 2028, valuation offers no cushion against a broken chart.

book_subsections.title: How Foreign Exchange and Treasury Yields Shape the Multiple
paragraphs: Two macro variables also sit quietly behind SKHY's valuation ceiling: the Korean won and U.S. Treasury yields. Because SK hynix sells HBM and enterprise SSDs primarily in U.S. dollars while incurring a substantial share of Korean fab labor, power, and construction expenses in won, a weaker won at 1,361.89 per dollar boosts reported KRW operating margins. Conversely, any sudden won appreciation toward 1,200 would trim translated domestic profits while making U.S. ADR parity even harder to justify.

At the same time, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield has climbed to 5.10% as of November 2026, up 20 basis points in a single week, while the 2-year yield sits at 4.86%. Higher long-end discount rates punish long-duration growth narratives and force equity investors to demand a wider margin of safety. When risk-free short-term Treasuries pay nearly 4.9%, paying 5.53 times book value for a capital-intensive memory ADR trading at a 43.6% premium to its Seoul home market simply does not clear an institutional hurdle.

Let us summarize the valuation lesson clearly for your mental model. Never judge a memory semiconductor stock by its trailing or forward P/E ratio alone, because earnings peak right before margins mean-revert. Always triangulate price-to-book against prior cycle bands, test Reverse DCF cash-flow assumptions against fab capex intensity, and—for foreign ADRs like SKHY—check the exact depositary ratio against the home exchange. On all three counts, $131.79 is far less cheap than its 3.25x forward P/E headline suggests.

Walk through one final sanity check on enterprise value. At $917.61 billion on Finviz, SKHY's enterprise value is larger than Micron's entire market capitalization ($880.6 billion) and nearly eight times Seagate ($121.27 billion) or Western Digital ($110.67 billion). Even on Seoul parity ($617.3 billion EV), SK hynix is priced as a mega-cap global semiconductor titan. When a stock already commands that scale, future returns depend on whether free cash flow compounds without a cyclical reset. With 2027 capex commitments rising in Cheongju, Yongin, and West Lafayette, Indiana, any deceleration in hyperscaler AI server orders will hit free cash flow faster than headline operating profit.

That is why our valuation verdict in Chapter 7 is clear: SKHY's 3.25x forward P/E is an optical peak-cycle multiple, while its 5.53x ADR price-to-book and 43.6% premium over KRX 000660 leave no margin of safety at $131.79.
